parts.title: Part A
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y elige la respuesta que mejor responde a la pregunta. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you want to keep going or stop here?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Let us call it a day.

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest?
questions.explanation: «Call it a day» = dar por terminada la jornada.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do you think the grant application has a chance?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Honestly, it is a long shot.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: It will take a long time.
questions.explanation: «A long shot» = con pocas probabilidades.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: What time does the seminar finish?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Off the top of my head, around four.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She is certain about the time.
She is answering from memory, without checking.
She did not hear the question.
questions.explanation: «Off the top of my head» = sin comprobarlo, de memoria.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Should we book the restaurant now?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Let us play it by ear.

questions.stem: What does the man prefer?
options: Deciding later, depending on how things go.
questions.explanation: «Play it by ear» = ir viendo sobre la marcha.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Are you ready for the exam?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I still need to brush up on the second unit.

questions.stem: What does the woman need to do?
questions.explanation: «Brush up on» = repasar algo que ya se estudió.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How is the new job treating you?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I am still learning the ropes.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: He is still learning how things work.
questions.explanation: «Learn the ropes» = aprender el funcionamiento de algo nuevo.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Did you understand the last part of the lecture?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I was completely lost.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She could not find the room.
questions.explanation: «Lost» aquí es no entender, no perderse físicamente.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Can you finish the report by Thursday?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It will be cutting it close.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: He will barely have enough time.
questions.explanation: «Cut it close» = llegar por muy poco.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: So what is the paper about, in short?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: In a nutshell, cities cool themselves badly.

questions.stem: What is the woman doing?
questions.explanation: «In a nutshell» = en pocas palabras.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You look exhausted.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I pulled an all-nighter.

questions.stem: What did the man do?
questions.explanation: «Pull an all-nighter» = pasar la noche en vela, normalmente estudiando.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Are you coming to the department dinner?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I will have to take a rain check.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She cannot come but would like to another time.
questions.explanation: «Take a rain check» = dejarlo para otra ocasión.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How is the thesis going?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I am in over my head, to be honest.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: The work is beyond what he can handle right now.
questions.explanation: «In over one's head» = sobrepasado.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Did the professor accept your excuse?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Let us say I am on thin ice.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She is in a risky position.
questions.explanation: «On thin ice» = en situación delicada.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Are you going to keep applying?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: I am not throwing in the towel yet.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «Throw in the towel» = rendirse.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you know what happened at the meeting?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Someone will bring me up to speed later.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: Someone will tell her what she missed.
questions.explanation: «Bring someone up to speed» = poner al día.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The scholarship application is complicated.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Still, it is worth a shot.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: It is a waste of time.
questions.explanation: «Worth a shot» = vale la pena intentarlo.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Why did she leave the company?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: The reorganisation was the last straw.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: It was the final problem that made her leave.
questions.explanation: «The last straw» = la gota que colmó el vaso.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Do you two agree on the method?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: We are finally on the same page.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: They are reading the same book.
They now understand it the same way.
questions.explanation: «On the same page» = de acuerdo, con el mismo entendimiento.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Did you enjoy the documentary?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I dozed off halfway through.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Doze off» = quedarse dormido.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Can I borrow your notes from Tuesday?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: They are yours, no strings attached.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
questions.explanation: «No strings attached» = sin condiciones.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Are the results in yet?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Beats me. Nobody has said anything.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Beats me» = ni idea.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I heard you are moving to the coast.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Where did you hear that? It is news to nobody but me.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
options: He had not heard about it himself.
questions.explanation: Ironía: se entera de su propia noticia por otra persona.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Is the library open during the break?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Only the ground floor, and only mornings.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the library?
options: It opens partially during the break.
questions.explanation: Abre, pero limitado: una planta y solo por las mañanas.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: You have been quiet about the results.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: There is not much to celebrate.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
questions.explanation: Litotes: decir poco para dar a entender que fue mal.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Should I email the professor again?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I would give her a couple of days.

questions.stem: What does the woman advise?
questions.explanation: Aconseja esperar, no insistir ahora.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Is the lab equipment reliable?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: It has been acting up all week.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: It is very old but reliable.
questions.explanation: «Act up» = funcionar mal, dar problemas.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Did you get the internship?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: I am still keeping my fingers crossed.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
questions.explanation: «Fingers crossed» = a la espera, con esperanza.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: How was the conference food?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Let us focus on the talks.

questions.stem: What does the man imply?
options: He did not attend the talks.
questions.explanation: Cambia de tema en vez de criticar: implica que no le gustó.

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Do you want to present first or last?

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: First, before I lose my nerve.

questions.stem: What does the woman mean?
options: She wants to present early to avoid getting nervous.
questions.explanation: «Lose one's nerve» = perder el valor.

script.speaker: Woman
script.text: Is the new schedule final?

script.speaker: Man
script.text: Pencil it in for now.

questions.stem: What does the man mean?
options: Note it provisionally; it may change.
questions.explanation: «Pencil it in» = anotarlo de forma provisional.

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I need to change my thesis supervisor and I do not know where to start.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: That is more common than you think. What is the reason?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: My topic drifted towards statistics and she works on fieldwork.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: So it is a question of fit, not a conflict.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Exactly. We get along fine.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: That makes it much easier. You need a signed form from both professors and a paragraph explaining the change.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Does the department have to approve it?

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: The committee sees it, but with both signatures it is a formality.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: And my defence date?

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: That is the part to watch. A new supervisor can ask for one extra semester, and you cannot appeal that.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: So I should ask about the timeline before signing anything.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Ask that first, and in writing.

questions.stem: Why does the student want to change supervisor?
options: She had an argument with her supervisor.
Her topic no longer matches her supervisor's field.
Her supervisor is leaving the university.
questions.explanation: Dice que el tema derivó hacia estadística y la directora trabaja en campo.

questions.stem: What does the adviser say about the committee?
options: It does not review the change at all.
With both signatures its approval is routine.
questions.explanation: «With both signatures it is a formality».

questions.stem: What does the adviser warn the student about?
options: The defence could be delayed by a semester.
She cannot keep her current topic.
questions.explanation: El nuevo director puede pedir un semestre más y no hay apelación.

questions.stem: What does the adviser recommend doing first?
options: Asking about the timeline in writing.
questions.explanation: «Ask that first, and in writing».

parts.title: Part B · Conversación 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la conversación y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I got an email saying my library account is blocked.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Let me look. Yes, there is an unreturned item from the reserve collection.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I returned everything before the break.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Reserve items go into a different drop box. If it went into the general one, it may still be in transit.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: It has been three weeks.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Then it was probably shelved in the wrong section rather than checked in.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Can you remove the block while you look for it?

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: I can suspend it for seven days. If the book does not appear, the charge comes back.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: And if it never appears?

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: You would pay a replacement fee, but you can contest it once with the receipt of your return.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I do not keep those receipts.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Most people do not. From now on, photograph the drop box screen.

questions.stem: Why is the student's account blocked?
options: She owes a late fee from last year.
A reserve item is registered as unreturned.
questions.explanation: Hay un ejemplar de la colección de reserva sin devolver.

questions.stem: What does the librarian suggest happened to the book?
options: It was stolen from the drop box.
It was sent to another campus.
It was shelved in the wrong section instead of checked in.
questions.explanation: Sugiere que se colocó mal en vez de registrarse la devolución.

questions.stem: What can the librarian do immediately?
options: Suspend the block for a week.
questions.explanation: «I can suspend it for seven days».

questions.stem: What advice does the librarian give for the future?
options: Return books at the front desk only.
Photograph the drop box screen as proof.
Keep paper receipts for a year.
questions.explanation: Le dice que fotografíe la pantalla del buzón.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 1
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Today I want to talk about why the metric system took so long to spread, because the usual answer, that people resist change, explains almost nothing.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: France adopted the metre in 1795 and then spent forty years failing to impose it on its own citizens. Markets kept using local units, and in 1812 the government legalised a hybrid system in which old names were attached to metric quantities.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The problem was not arithmetic. It was that old units were tied to the work. A unit of land was often defined as what one person could plough in a day, which encoded soil quality and slope. Replacing it with an abstract area threw that information away.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Metric units won when the state gained reasons to measure the same thing everywhere: taxation, conscription, railways. Where central administration was weak, adoption was slow regardless of how rational the system was.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: So the lesson is that a measurement system is not only a language. It is a claim about who has the right to define the quantity, and that is what was really being negotiated.

questions.stem: What is the main point of the talk?
options: The metric system is arithmetically superior.
Metric adoption depended on state power, not on rationality.
France abandoned the metric system in 1812.
Local units were more accurate than metric ones.
questions.explanation: La tesis es que la adopción dependió de la administración central.

questions.stem: What does the professor say about old units of land?
options: They were invented by the state.
They were more precise than metric units.
They encoded information about the land itself.
questions.explanation: Codificaban calidad del suelo y pendiente.

questions.stem: What happened in 1812?
options: A hybrid system with old names was legalised.
questions.explanation: El gobierno legalizó un sistema híbrido.

questions.stem: According to the professor, what was really being negotiated?
options: The exact length of the metre.
Who had the authority to define quantities.
questions.explanation: Cierra diciendo que se negociaba el derecho a definir la cantidad.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 2
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The deep-sea floor was assumed to be a desert until the 1970s, and the reasoning behind that assumption was perfectly sound at the time.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: No sunlight reaches those depths, so no photosynthesis. Everything eaten down there had to fall from above, and what falls is scarce. A square metre of abyssal plain receives a few grams of organic material a year.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Then a submersible near the Galapagos found dense clusters of clams and tube worms around hot vents, with a biomass comparable to a shallow reef. The food chain there begins with bacteria that oxidise hydrogen sulphide.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Notice what changed and what did not. The energy still comes from outside the organism; it is simply chemical rather than solar. The old reasoning was not wrong about scarcity, only about the sources available.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: This is worth remembering when you read that a discovery overturned everything. Usually it does not. It adds one term to an equation that was otherwise correct.

questions.stem: Why was the deep-sea floor assumed to be nearly lifeless?
options: The water pressure kills all organisms.
Without sunlight, food had to sink from above and was scarce.
The temperature is too low for life.
No one had ever explored it.
questions.explanation: Sin luz no hay fotosíntesis y lo que cae es escaso.

questions.stem: What did the submersible near the Galapagos find?
options: A new species of fish only.
questions.explanation: Encontró densas agrupaciones de almejas y gusanos tubícolas.

questions.stem: What begins the food chain at the vents?
questions.explanation: Bacterias que oxidan sulfuro de hidrógeno.

questions.stem: What broader point does the professor make at the end?
options: The old theory was completely wrong.
Discoveries usually add to existing reasoning rather than overturn it.
Deep-sea research is more important than surface research.
questions.explanation: Suele añadirse un término a una ecuación que ya era correcta.

parts.title: Part C · Charla 3
parts.instructions: Escucha la charla y responde a las preguntas. Suena una sola vez.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: I want to describe an experiment about how people judge the length of a wait, because the result is more useful than it first appears.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: An airport received complaints about baggage delay. The walk from the gate to the carousel took one minute; the bags then took seven. The airport moved the arrival gates further away, so the walk took six minutes and the bags took two.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: Total time was unchanged. Complaints fell to almost nothing.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The standard explanation is that occupied time feels shorter than unoccupied time. That is true, but incomplete. Notice that the passengers were also making progress. Walking towards the bags feels like part of getting them; standing at a belt does not.

script.speaker: Professor
script.text: The practical implication is not to make people walk more. It is that when you cannot make a process faster, you can often make the waiting part of the work rather than an interruption to it.

questions.stem: What change did the airport make?
options: It moved arrival gates further from the carousel.
It reduced the total waiting time.
It added seating at the carousel.
questions.explanation: Alejó las puertas de llegada.

questions.stem: What happened to the total time?
questions.explanation: «Total time was unchanged».

questions.stem: Why does the professor call the standard explanation incomplete?
options: It ignores the sense of making progress.
It was based on a single airport.
questions.explanation: Añade que los pasajeros además avanzaban hacia el objetivo.

questions.stem: What is the practical implication?
options: Make the waiting feel like part of the process.
questions.explanation: Convertir la espera en parte del trabajo, no en una interrupción.

parts.title: Structure
parts.instructions: Elige la opción que completa la frase correctamente.

questions.stem: Rarely ______ a species recover once its breeding population falls below a few dozen.
questions.explanation: «Rarely» al principio exige inversión: auxiliar + sujeto («does a species recover»).

questions.stem: The report, ______ conclusions were disputed, was withdrawn three months later.
questions.explanation: Posesivo relativo: «whose conclusions».

questions.stem: ______ the storm damaged the antenna, the station kept broadcasting.
questions.explanation: Ante oración completa va conjunción: «although». «Despite» exige sustantivo.

questions.stem: The technique is useful ______ the sample remains frozen.
questions.explanation: «Provided that» = siempre que, condicional formal.

questions.stem: Not until the second trial ______ the side effect.
questions.explanation: «Not until» al inicio fuerza inversión con auxiliar.

questions.stem: The committee recommended that the deadline ______ by two weeks.
questions.explanation: Subjuntivo tras «recommend that»: verbo en forma base.

questions.stem: ______ of the two methods produces reliable results with small samples.
questions.explanation: «Neither» para dos elementos.

questions.stem: The glacier has retreated ______ than it did during the previous century.
questions.explanation: «Far» intensifica el comparativo: far more rapidly.

questions.stem: ______ enough funding, the project would have finished on schedule.
questions.explanation: Condicional del tercer tipo invertido: «Had there been».

questions.stem: The author spent a decade ______ the manuscript before publishing it.
questions.explanation: «Spend time + -ing».

questions.stem: The results were consistent ______ those obtained in the pilot study.
questions.explanation: «Consistent with» es la colocación correcta.

questions.stem: Hardly had the session begun ______ the connection failed.
questions.explanation: Correlación fija: hardly … when.

questions.stem: The instrument, ______ in 1908, is still in working order.
questions.explanation: Participio pasado reducido: «(which was) built in 1908».

questions.stem: Few economists ______ that the estimate was too optimistic.
questions.explanation: «Few economists» es plural contable: verbo en plural.

questions.stem: The larger the sample, ______ the margin of error.
questions.explanation: Estructura correlativa: the + comparativo, the + comparativo.

parts.title: Written Expression
parts.instructions: Identifica la parte subrayada que hay que corregir.

questions.stem: (A) Each of the samples were (B) analysed (C) twice (D) to reduce error.
questions.explanation: «Each» es singular: was analysed.

questions.stem: (A) The criteria was published (B) in advance (C) on the website (D) of the department.
questions.explanation: «Criteria» es el plural de «criterion»: were published.

questions.stem: (A) Despite of (B) the delay, (C) the crew completed (D) the survey.
questions.explanation: «Despite» no lleva «of»: despite the delay.

questions.stem: (A) The professor asked us to not (B) submit (C) the draft (D) before Friday.
options: The professor asked us to not
questions.explanation: El orden es «not to submit».

questions.stem: (A) Neither (B) the director nor (C) the assistants (D) was informed of the change.
questions.explanation: Con «neither…nor» el verbo concuerda con el sujeto más cercano: were informed.

questions.stem: (A) The amount of (B) students enrolled (C) has risen (D) sharply.
questions.explanation: «Students» es contable: the number of.

questions.stem: (A) She is (B) one of (C) the few researchers (D) who has access to the archive.
options: who has access to the archive
questions.explanation: El antecedente de «who» es «researchers»: who have.

questions.stem: (A) The findings were (B) more significant (C) that those (D) of the earlier study.
questions.explanation: Comparativo con «than», no «that».

questions.stem: (A) Having finished (B) the experiment, (C) the equipment was (D) cleaned and stored.
questions.explanation: Participio colgante: el equipo no terminó el experimento.

questions.stem: (A) The lecture was (B) so interesting (C) that hardly (D) nobody left before the end.
questions.explanation: Doble negación: «hardly» ya es negativo, así que va «hardly anybody».

questions.stem: (A) A number of participants has (B) withdrawn (C) from the programme (D) since March.
questions.explanation: «A number of» es plural: participants have withdrawn.

questions.stem: (A) The theory (B) which he proposed it (C) in 1954 (D) remains influential.
questions.explanation: Pronombre reasuntivo: sobra «it» dentro de la relativa.

questions.stem: (A) Scientists have long (B) been interested (C) on how (D) birds navigate.
questions.explanation: «Interested in», no «interested on».

questions.stem: (A) If the sensor (B) would fail, (C) the backup (D) takes over automatically.
questions.explanation: En la condicional no va «would»: if the sensor fails.

questions.stem: (A) The museum (B) has recently acquired (C) three paintings (D) which are dated from 1620.
questions.explanation: «Date from» no es pasiva: which date from 1620.

questions.stem: (A) Most of the equipment (B) in the laboratories (C) are new, (D) although the building is not.
questions.explanation: «Equipment» es incontable: is new.

questions.stem: (A) He explained (B) the committee (C) that the deadline (D) could not be moved.
questions.explanation: «Explain» exige preposición: explained to the committee.

questions.stem: (A) The city has (B) twice as many (C) inhabitants (D) than it had in 1950.
questions.explanation: Con «as many as» va «as»: as it had in 1950.

questions.stem: (A) Between 1890 and 1910, (B) the population (C) has grown (D) by a third.
questions.explanation: Periodo cerrado en el pasado: grew, no has grown.

questions.stem: (A) The results, (B) that were published (C) last month, (D) confirm the hypothesis.
questions.explanation: En relativa explicativa se usa «which», no «that».

questions.stem: (A) Only after the deadline (B) the department (C) announced (D) the new criteria.
questions.explanation: «Only after» exige inversión: did the department announce.

questions.stem: (A) There is (B) considerable evidences (C) that the practice (D) began much earlier.
questions.explanation: «Evidence» es incontable: no lleva plural.

questions.stem: (A) Everyone agreed (B) with what (C) the technician (D) suggested to do about the calibration.
options: suggested to do about the calibration
questions.explanation: «Suggest» no rige infinitivo: suggested doing.

questions.stem: (A) Although (B) the survey was thorough, (C) but the sample (D) was too small.
questions.explanation: «Although» y «but» no se combinan: sobra «but».

questions.stem: (A) The two theories (B) differ (C) each other (D) in one crucial respect.
questions.explanation: «Differ from each other»: falta la preposición.

parts.title: Texto 1
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, the standard account of how children learn vocabulary was that they hear a word, are shown its referent, and store the pair. The account is not wrong, but it cannot be the whole story, because the arithmetic does not work. A six-year-old knows roughly ten thousand words. Explicit teaching of that many pairs, at the rate parents actually manage, would take decades.

The gap is closed by a mechanism usually called fast mapping. Presented with a novel word in a context containing one unfamiliar object among several familiar ones, children as young as two assign the word to the unfamiliar object after a single exposure, and retain the assignment for weeks. They are not learning the meaning so much as reserving a slot for it.

What makes this efficient is that the initial assignment is provisional. A child who first hears 'dog' applied to a neighbour's spaniel will happily extend it to other four-legged animals, then narrow the category as corrections arrive. Errors of over-extension are therefore not failures of the system; they are the system working, since a guess that is too broad is cheap to correct while a guess that is too narrow may never be tested.

The mechanism has limits that are easy to overlook. It works well for concrete nouns and poorly for verbs, whose referents are events rather than things and cannot be pointed at. It also depends on the child already knowing the other objects in the scene, which is why vocabulary growth accelerates rather than proceeding at a constant rate.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To criticise parents for teaching too few words.
To compare vocabulary learning in children and adults.
To explain a mechanism that accounts for rapid vocabulary growth.
To argue that children learn words one pair at a time.
questions.explanation: Presenta el fast mapping como explicación del ritmo de aprendizaje.

questions.stem: Why does the author say the traditional account 'cannot be the whole story'?
options: Children rarely look at what adults point to.
The number of words known exceeds what explicit teaching could supply.
Parents do not teach vocabulary at all.
The account was disproved in the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: «The arithmetic does not work»: diez mil palabras no caben en la enseñanza explícita.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what do children do when they hear a novel word?
options: They ask an adult for a definition.
They ignore it until they hear it again.
They assign it to the most familiar object.
They assign it to the unfamiliar object present.
questions.explanation: Lo asignan al objeto desconocido de la escena.

questions.stem: The phrase 'reserving a slot for it' suggests that the child
options: creates a placeholder to be refined later.
memorises the exact meaning at once.
questions.explanation: El significado queda pendiente de afinarse: es un hueco reservado.

questions.stem: How long do children retain a fast-mapped assignment?
questions.explanation: El texto dice «retain the assignment for weeks».

questions.stem: How does the author interpret over-extension errors?
options: As a sign of delayed development.
As evidence that the mechanism is working.
As proof that fast mapping fails.
As a result of poor parental correction.
questions.explanation: «They are the system working».

questions.stem: Why is a guess that is too narrow described as worse?
options: It requires more corrections from adults.
It is harder for children to remember.
It may never be tested and therefore never corrected.
questions.explanation: Una categoría estrecha no se pone a prueba, así que no se corrige.

questions.stem: Why does fast mapping work poorly for verbs?
options: Their referents are events and cannot be pointed at.
Verbs are heard less often than nouns.
questions.explanation: Los referentes son eventos, no cosas señalables.

questions.stem: What does the passage say explains the acceleration of vocabulary growth?
options: Children are taught more words as they age.
Fast mapping depends on already knowing the other objects present.
Adults speak more slowly to older children.
questions.explanation: Cuantas más palabras se saben, mejor funciona el mecanismo.

questions.stem: The word 'provisional' in the third paragraph is closest in meaning to

parts.title: Texto 2
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
The commercial ice trade of the nineteenth century is a useful case study in how an industry can be destroyed by success rather than by failure. Between 1830 and 1880, blocks cut from New England ponds were shipped to Calcutta, Havana and Rio de Janeiro, insulated with sawdust in the holds of returning cargo ships. Losses in transit ran near thirty per cent, which was acceptable because the raw material cost nothing beyond the labour of cutting it.

The trade created its own market. Households that had never used ice acquired iceboxes, and by 1870 the domestic demand of American cities dwarfed the exotic export routes that had made the industry famous. Breweries, meatpackers and hospitals became dependent on a supply that arrived by cart on a fixed schedule.

That dependence is what killed the harvesters. A customer who merely wants ice can wait for winter; a customer whose business stops without it cannot. When mechanical refrigeration became reliable in the 1880s, it was more expensive per unit than pond ice, and the harvesters said so, correctly. What they missed was that their large customers were no longer buying ice. They were buying certainty, and a warm winter or a polluted pond could interrupt the natural supply in a way that a machine could not.

The industry did not vanish at once. It contracted from the top, losing the industrial accounts first and surviving in rural households into the 1920s. By then the skills, the tools and the insurance markets that had supported large-scale harvesting were gone, and the recovery that some owners waited for was no longer physically possible.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Mechanical refrigeration was cheaper than harvested ice.
The ice trade failed because of poor transport methods.
Exports to tropical ports were never profitable.
The ice trade was undone by the dependence its own growth created.
questions.explanation: La tesis: el éxito generó una dependencia que el hielo natural no podía garantizar.

questions.stem: Why were transit losses of thirty per cent acceptable?
options: The raw material itself cost nothing.
Customers paid for the lost ice.
The losses were later reduced to zero.
questions.explanation: El costo era solo la mano de obra del corte.

questions.stem: By 1870, what was the largest source of demand?
options: Households and businesses in American cities.
questions.explanation: La demanda doméstica superaba con mucho a la exportación.

questions.stem: What distinction does the author draw between types of customer?
options: Those who pay in advance and those who pay later.
Those who can wait for ice and those whose business stops without it.
Customers in cold climates and warm climates.
questions.explanation: Es la distinción central del tercer párrafo.

questions.stem: The harvesters' claim about the cost of refrigeration is described as
questions.explanation: «The harvesters said so, correctly», pero se equivocaban de asunto.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what were large customers actually buying?
questions.explanation: «They were buying certainty».

questions.stem: What could interrupt the natural supply?
options: A warm winter or a polluted pond.
questions.explanation: Son los dos ejemplos que da el texto.

questions.stem: How did the industry decline?
options: It lost industrial customers first and rural ones last.
questions.explanation: «It contracted from the top».

questions.stem: Why was recovery impossible by the 1920s?
options: The ponds had all been drained.
Consumers preferred the taste of machine ice.
The supporting skills, tools and insurance markets had disappeared.
questions.explanation: Lo dice el último párrafo.

questions.stem: The word 'dwarfed' in the second paragraph is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: «Dwarf» = empequeñecer por comparación, superar con mucho.

parts.title: Texto 3
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Desert plants are often described as storing water, and some do, but the more common strategy is subtler: they manage the timing of loss. Every plant faces the same trade-off, since the pores that admit carbon dioxide for photosynthesis also release water vapour. In a temperate climate the exchange is cheap. In a desert it can be fatal.

One solution is to invert the schedule. Plants using crassulacean acid metabolism open their pores at night, when the air is cool and humid, fix carbon dioxide into an organic acid, and store the acid until morning. During the day the pores stay shut and photosynthesis proceeds on the stored supply. Water loss falls by up to ninety per cent compared with the ordinary pathway.

The cost is speed. The acid store is finite, so carbon fixation stops when it is exhausted, usually by early afternoon. These plants grow slowly and cannot exploit a wet season quickly. Where rainfall is unpredictable but occasionally generous, they are outcompeted by annuals that germinate, flower and die within a few weeks, leaving seeds to wait out the drought.

This is why the vegetation of a desert is rarely uniform. The two strategies succeed under different rainfall patterns, and most deserts contain patches of each. A survey that samples only after a wet season will find annuals and conclude the desert is productive; one that samples in a dry year will find succulents and conclude the opposite. Both are describing the same place.

questions.stem: What is the main point of the passage?
options: All desert plants store water in their tissues.
Desert plants use different strategies suited to different rainfall patterns.
Annual plants are superior to succulents.
questions.explanation: El texto contrasta dos estrategias y explica cuándo gana cada una.

questions.stem: What trade-off does every plant face?
options: Growing tall means producing fewer seeds.
Admitting carbon dioxide also means losing water vapour.
Storing water means storing less sugar.
Opening pores at night means colder tissues.
questions.explanation: Los mismos poros que admiten CO2 dejan salir vapor de agua.

questions.stem: When do plants using crassulacean acid metabolism open their pores?
questions.explanation: De noche, cuando el aire está fresco y húmedo.

questions.stem: What is stored until morning?
options: An organic acid containing fixed carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: Fijan el CO2 en un ácido orgánico y lo guardan.

questions.stem: By how much can this strategy reduce water loss?
options: By up to ninety per cent.
questions.explanation: El texto da la cifra explícitamente.

questions.stem: What is the disadvantage of the strategy?
options: The plants cannot survive cold nights.
Carbon fixation stops when the acid store runs out.
The pores are damaged by sunlight.
It requires more water in total.
questions.explanation: El almacén es finito y se agota, normalmente a primera hora de la tarde.

questions.stem: Under what conditions do annuals outcompete these plants?
options: When rainfall is steady all year.
When the soil is permanently wet.
When rainfall is unpredictable but occasionally generous.
questions.explanation: Es la condición que menciona el tercer párrafo.

questions.stem: What do annuals leave behind to survive the drought?
questions.explanation: «Leaving seeds to wait out the drought».

questions.stem: What problem with surveys does the author identify?
options: Deserts cannot be sampled reliably at all.
The timing of sampling can produce opposite conclusions.
Most surveys use the wrong equipment.
questions.explanation: Muestrear tras lluvia o en año seco da conclusiones contrarias del mismo sitio.

questions.stem: The word 'exhausted' in the third paragraph is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Aquí significa agotado en el sentido de consumido.

parts.title: Texto 4
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
The invention of the index is usually treated as a minor episode in the history of the book, which underestimates how much it changed reading. Before the thirteenth century, a European scholar who wanted a passage had essentially two options: remember where it was, or read until it appeared. Manuscripts were continuous, unpaginated and often unpunctuated.

The alphabetical index emerged from an institutional need rather than a scholarly one. Preaching orders required friars to compose sermons on assigned topics at short notice, drawing on authorities they could not possibly have memorised. Concordances listing every occurrence of a word were compiled for this purpose, one of them requiring the coordinated labour of some five hundred friars.

Alphabetical order was not the obvious choice it now seems. Contemporaries objected that it was arbitrary, scattering related ideas across the list and placing trivial entries beside important ones. Systematic arrangements by subject were considered more rational, and they were, for a reader who already knew the structure of the field. The advantage of alphabetical order is precisely that it requires no such knowledge, which is why it won.

The consequence was a new way of using books. A text could now be entered at any point and consulted rather than read, and authors began writing with that in mind, adding headings and summaries. The book stopped being something one went through and became something one went into.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Alphabetical order is the most rational arrangement.
Preaching orders invented the modern book.
The index changed how books were written and used.
questions.explanation: El cierre lo resume: cambió la forma de usar y escribir libros.

questions.stem: Before the thirteenth century, how did a scholar locate a passage?
options: By memory or by reading until reaching it.
questions.explanation: El texto da exactamente esas dos opciones.

questions.stem: What prompted the creation of alphabetical concordances?
options: A royal decree on book production.
The need to compose sermons on assigned topics quickly.
questions.explanation: Fue una necesidad institucional de las órdenes predicadoras.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the scale of the work?
options: It was done by a single scholar over a lifetime.
One concordance required about five hundred friars.
It took two years and cost a fortune.
The passage does not mention scale.
questions.explanation: Cita la cifra de unos quinientos frailes.

questions.stem: What objection was raised against alphabetical order?
options: It was too difficult to compile.
It separated related ideas and levelled important and trivial entries.
questions.explanation: Se le reprochaba ser arbitrario.

questions.stem: For which reader were systematic arrangements genuinely better?
options: One who already knew the structure of the field.
One who was learning to read.
One without access to a library.
questions.explanation: El texto concede que eran más racionales para ese lector.

questions.stem: Why did alphabetical order prevail?
options: It was ordered by the church.
It requires no prior knowledge of the subject.
It preserved the structure of the field.
questions.explanation: «It requires no such knowledge, which is why it won».

questions.stem: How did authors respond to the new way of reading?
questions.explanation: Empezaron a escribir pensando en la consulta.

questions.stem: The final sentence contrasts
options: reading a book through with consulting parts of it.
questions.explanation: «Went through» frente a «went into».

questions.stem: The word 'arbitrary' in the third paragraph is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Arbitrario: sin criterio de fondo.

parts.title: Texto 5
parts.instructions: Lee el texto y responde a las preguntas.
parts.passage:
Volcanic eruptions can cool the planet, but only under conditions narrow enough that most eruptions do nothing at all. The cooling agent is not ash, which falls out within weeks, but sulphur dioxide, which converts in the atmosphere into droplets that reflect sunlight. For that to matter, the gas must reach the stratosphere, above the weather that would otherwise wash it out.

This sets a threshold. An eruption may eject enormous volumes of rock and still have no measurable climatic effect if its plume stays low or its magma is poor in sulphur. Conversely, a moderate eruption rich in sulphur and vigorous enough to punch through the tropopause can lower global temperatures by several tenths of a degree for two or three years.

Latitude matters as much as size. Stratospheric circulation carries material from the tropics towards both poles, so a tropical eruption spreads its droplets over the whole planet. The same eruption at high latitude stays largely within one hemisphere, and its effect on global average temperature is correspondingly smaller, though regional effects can be severe.

Because of this, the historical record is easy to misread. Chronicles describing a terrible year following a distant eruption may be recording a coincidence, while eruptions that did alter the climate sometimes left no local impression at all, having occurred in places where nobody was writing anything down.

questions.stem: What is the main point of the passage?
options: All large eruptions cool the planet.
Volcanic ash is the main cause of cooling.
Only eruptions meeting specific conditions affect global climate.
Historical chronicles are the best record of eruptions.
questions.explanation: El texto insiste en las condiciones estrechas que hacen falta.

questions.stem: Why is ash not the cooling agent?
options: It absorbs rather than reflects sunlight.
It falls out of the atmosphere within weeks.
It is produced in very small amounts.
questions.explanation: Precipita en semanas.

questions.stem: What does sulphur dioxide form in the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Se convierte en gotitas reflectantes.

questions.stem: Why must the gas reach the stratosphere?
options: Below it, weather would wash the gas out.
The gas cannot form droplets lower down.
questions.explanation: Por debajo, la meteorología lo elimina.

questions.stem: What can prevent a very large eruption from affecting climate?
options: A low plume or magma poor in sulphur.
questions.explanation: Son las dos condiciones que menciona el texto.

questions.stem: How much can a suitable moderate eruption cool the planet?
options: By several degrees for a decade.
By several tenths of a degree for two or three years.
questions.explanation: La cifra aparece en el segundo párrafo.

questions.stem: Why does a tropical eruption have a wider effect?
options: The tropopause is lower in the tropics.
Stratospheric circulation carries material towards both poles.
questions.explanation: La circulación estratosférica reparte el material hacia ambos hemisferios.

questions.stem: What is true of high-latitude eruptions?
options: Their global effect is smaller but regional effects can be severe.
They have no effect of any kind.
They cool the planet more than tropical ones.
questions.explanation: El texto lo dice explícitamente.

questions.stem: Why is the historical record easy to misread?
options: Chronicles were usually written centuries later.
Bad years may coincide with eruptions that did not cause them.
questions.explanation: Advierte tanto de coincidencias como de erupciones sin testigos.

questions.stem: The word 'threshold' in the second paragraph is closest in meaning to
options: minimum level required for an effect
questions.explanation: Umbral: el mínimo a partir del cual algo ocurre.
